Figgy Pudding

Served at: Twelfth Night

Serves 8Prep 30 minCook 4 hours

Figgy pudding is a traditional British steamed dessert made with dried figs and a mixture of dried fruits, spices, and suet. It is famously served during Twelfth Night, marking the end of the Christmas season, and is often enjoyed with brandy butter or cream to celebrate the festive occasion.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (150g) dried figs, chopped
  • 1 cup (150g) raisins
  • 1 cup (150g) currants
  • 1 cup (120g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup (100g) fresh white breadcrumbs
  • 1/2 cup (100g) brown sugar
  • 1/2 cup (115g) suet (beef or vegetable)
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) milk
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/2 cup (120ml) dark molasses or treacle
  • 1 teaspoon baking powder
  • 1 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cloves
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • Zest of 1 lemon
  • Zest of 1 orange
  • 1/4 cup (60ml) brandy or dark rum, plus extra for flaming
  • Butter for greasing pudding basin

Method

  1. Grease a 2-quart (2-liter) pudding basin with butter and line the bottom with a circle of parchment paper.
  2. In a large bowl, combine the chopped figs, raisins, currants, flour, breadcrumbs, brown sugar, suet, baking powder, spices, salt, lemon zest, and orange zest. Mix well.
  3. In a separate bowl, whisk together the milk, eggs, molasses, and brandy or rum.
  4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until fully combined.
  5. Spoon the mixture into the prepared pudding basin, pressing down lightly to remove air pockets.
  6. Cover the basin with a double layer of greased parchment paper and then a layer of foil, securing tightly with kitchen string.
  7. Place the pudding basin in a large pot with a rack or folded towel at the bottom to prevent direct heat. Pour boiling water halfway up the sides of the basin.
  8. Cover the pot with a lid and steam the pudding for 4 hours, checking occasionally to ensure the water level remains high, adding more boiling water as needed.
  9. Once cooked, remove the pudding from the pot and let it cool. It can be stored wrapped in a cool place for several weeks to mature the flavors.
  10. To serve, re-steam the pudding for 1 hour. Warm some brandy, pour it over the pudding, and carefully ignite it to flame, then serve with brandy butter or cream.

Tips

  • For a vegetarian version, use vegetable suet or grated cold butter instead of beef suet.
  • Make the pudding several weeks in advance to allow the flavors to mature and deepen.
  • If steaming is not possible, the pudding can be baked in a water bath at 325°F (160°C) for about 3 hours, covered tightly with foil.
